title: Design System: Quranic Universal Audio — Inspector

display.purpose: Page-level titles. The size ceiling for chrome (32px).

body.purpose: Workhorse UI text: table rows, controls, descriptions (13.5–14px).

label.purpose: Metadata, counts, timing readouts, technical chips. Tabular numerals.

arabic.purpose: Quranic text and reciter names in embedded DigitalKhatt, RTL, larger than chrome.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The ONLY shadow. Keyboard focus / active control. Never elevation.

narrative.overview: Inspector is a precision instrument that refuses to shout. Underneath runs an enormous engine — hundreds of reciters across many deliveries, a 60fps loop synchronizing thousands of word/letter/phoneme boundaries against a playhead, validation, audit, releases. The visual system's job is to make none of it feel heavy: the surface is dark, still, and legible; the data is alive. One language, three moods — Dashboard orients and invites, Timestamps calms and reveals, Segments equips and disappears. The vocabulary is identical across all three; only density and stillness shift.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by conviction — built for multi-hour review and relaxed listening; no flash-of-light, no white modals.
Flat tonal layering, zero decorative shadow; depth is a five-step surface ramp.
One restrained cyan accent — rarity is the point.
OKLCH throughout; system fonts for chrome, one embedded Arabic face for Quranic text.
Calm scales with complexity: the busier the engine, the stiller the surface.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Exactly one accent: cyan, marking what is interactive or current. A second saturated hue that isn't a defined state color is a bug. Buttons do not get their own colors.

rules.name: The Hue-Plus-Label Rule
rules.body: State is never communicated by color alone. Every state hue ships with a text label and survives grayscale and color-blindness.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: Type sizes are a fixed ladder (11.5 · 13.5 · 14 · 16 · 22 · 32), not fluid clamps. Consistent DPI in panels means a shrinking heading looks worse, not better.

rules.name: The Arabic-Is-The-Subject Rule
rules.body: Quranic text and reciter names render in the DigitalKhatt Arabic face, larger than surroundings, correct bidi — never a caption, never transliteration alone.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and on hover. The single allowed shadow is the accent focus ring. Drop-shadows are forbidden; step up the surface ramp instead.

dos: Do consume tokens via var(--token) for every new surface — colors, --s-* spacing, --r-1/2/3 radii, --fs-* sizes, --t-*/--ease-* motion.
Do keep exactly one accent (cyan); mark interactive and current state with it and nothing else.
Do convey depth with the surface ramp: canvas → panel → panel-2 → elevated, wells to canvas-inset.
Do pair every state hue with a text label and verify it survives grayscale.
Do render reciter names and Quranic text in the DigitalKhatt Arabic face, larger than chrome, with correct RTL/bidi.
Do hold transitions to 120–200ms and degrade to instant under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
Do let busier surfaces get quieter: on Timestamps every pixel of motion or color must serve comprehension or calm.
donts: Don't introduce Material-Design button colors (#4361ee, #2e7d32, #6d1a1a, #6a1b9a) or any per-button palette. The live app's legacy Material buttons are drift, not the system.
Don't hardcode hex, off-scale radii (4px, 6px, 10px, 12px), or ad-hoc rem font sizes; snap to the token scales.
Don't add decorative shadows or glassmorphism; the only shadow is the accent focus ring.
Don't use a border-left/border-right colored stripe on cards, rows, or callouts.
Don't ship a hero-metric block or an identical icon-headline-text card grid; let the catalog carry the scale.
Don't decorate the religious content: no green-and-gold, no arabesque borders, no calligraphic flourish as ornament.
Don't let the Timestamps surface shout — no visualizer flash, neon EQ, or motion competing with the recitation.
Don't drop body text below text-muted, or use color as the only state signal.
